relatedNotes.label: When Has the Land Really Changed?

title: Reservoir water extent and hydroperiod
summary: Compare where water was present, where a shoreline shifted between observations, and how long an area remained inundated. Three complementary GeoTIFF deposits support these different questions.
coverage: Polyphytos, Greece (inundation maps: 2021-2022); Polyphytos and Giaretta, Italy (transition and hydroperiod periods are specified in the files)
creators: Ioannis Manakos; Afroditi Kita; Christos Kalogeropoulos.
contribution: WQeMS raster products developed with the CERTH team using Copernicus Sentinel-2 observations.
access: Public GeoTIFF datasets. Read each deposit's class definitions and NoData conventions before comparing layers.
reuse: All three linked deposits: CC BY 4.0. Cite the particular dataset used.

relatedNotes.label: Why Do Shorelines Move Between Satellite Observations?

title: Wetland inundation and hydroperiod
summary: Explore water extent at individual observation dates and estimated inundation duration across three protected wetlands. The maps include INSPIRE metadata to help identify and interpret the products.
coverage: Doñana: 2015-2017; Camargue: 2016-2018; Danube Delta: 2016-2017. Hydroperiod products cover the specified hydrological years.
contribution: ECOPOTENTIAL wetland-mapping products from the CERTH team.
access: Public raster datasets and metadata. Hydroperiod is estimated between observations, not measured continuously each day.
reuse: All six linked deposits: CC BY 4.0. Cite the site-specific products used.

relatedNotes.label: Can Earth Observation Describe Ecological Condition?

title: Abrupt vegetation-cycle changes in Doñana
summary: Locate breaks in the NDVI time series of Doñana marshes. The layers record the timing and number of detected changes, offering a starting point for investigating changes in vegetation behaviour.
creators: Georgios Kordelas; Ioannis Manakos; Kalliroi Marini; Vasileios Kotsias; Michail Papanastasiou.
contribution: ECOPOTENTIAL change-detection products derived with BFAST time-series analysis.
access: Public raster layers with accompanying metadata. A detected break does not, on its own, identify its ecological cause.
reuse: CC BY 4.0. Cite the dataset and the method where appropriate.

relatedNotes.label: Separating Seasonal Forest Change from Disturbance

title: Seasonal vegetation metrics in Doñana
summary: Examine the timing of green-up, senescence and peak NDVI, together with the number of seasonal peaks. Classification layers group areas with similar vegetation-cycle characteristics.
coverage: Doñana marshes, Spain; December 2015 to November 2016
creators: Ioannis Manakos; Georgios Kordelas; Kalliroi Marini; Georgios Chantziaras.
contribution: ECOPOTENTIAL phenology layers produced from NDVI time series using Phenex.
access: Public metric and classification layers with INSPIRE metadata. The repository title contains an invalid November end-day; the coverage is stated here by month.
reuse: CC BY 4.0. Preserve the dataset citation when reusing the layers.

title: Landscape structure across protected areas
summary: Explore habitat-area and fragmentation measures, including patch density and effective mesh size. Raster layers and per-object tables describe landscape structure rather than directly counting species.
coverage: Samaria: selected years 1985-2015; Montado: 2007 and 2012; Prespa: 2012; Curonian Lagoon: 2013-2014; La Palma: 2007; Sierra Nevada: three input vegetation maps
contribution: ECOPOTENTIAL landscape and biodiversity-indicator products derived from land-cover and habitat maps.
access: Public raster products, indicator tables and metadata. Each site's input maps and spatial units should be checked before cross-site comparison.
reuse: All six linked deposits: CC BY 4.0. Cite each site's dataset separately.
